mentions.text:
Everyone is about to make the same mistake on SpaceX.

The most hyped IPO of the decade is coming, and retail will treat day one like the entry. It is the exit, at least for a while.

Look at what actually happened to the last five hyped IPOs. Robinhood dropped 92% from its IPO. Coinbase 93%. Rivian 95%. Uber 70%. The hype was priced in before retail ever clicked buy. Day-one buyers held the bag for one to two years.

Think of an IPO like a party that peaks the moment you walk in. The valuation already assumes the best version of the story. There is nowhere to go but down until the business catches up to the price.

Then the real money showed up at the bottom, when nobody wanted these names. Robinhood is now ~22x off its low. Uber ~7.4x off its low. It pays to be patient, especially when there is so much hype around these names.

Plus, this only works if the business delivers. Sometimes they don't.

Look at Rivian for instance. It trades at ~0.2x its IPO price four years later. I don't think this will be the case for SpaceX, but it's best to know all the possible outcomes.

I am not chasing the open.

If SpaceX is the business everyone believes, there will be a better price on a macro bad tape.

I'll own this name, but not on day 1. It pays to be first, but it pays more to be in the right place at the right time.

为什么市场会关注 SpaceX？

因为它不是一个普通概念。

它背后是 SpaceX、Starlink、火箭发射、卫星互联网、国防航天、AI 数据传输入口，以及马斯克这个天然流量源。

这些东西叠在一起，导致 SPCX 很容易成为市场上的超级交易标的。

更关键的是，SPCX 有一个很重要的价格锚。

它在哪个价格完成 IPO，市场自然就会把那个位置当成一个参考区间。

价格一旦回到这些地方，就容易出现自然买盘。

————————

这和很多加密货币不一样。

Crypto 跌下来，大家只能问“情绪还在不在”。

但 SPCX 跌下来，市场会问的是：

这个价格是不是接近 IPO 成本区？

这个位置是不是有人愿意重新接？

我很早就在 SPCX 150 美元附近看到它积累了最多的负向 Gamma。（币安直播间提醒过多次）

这意味着当价格跌到 150 附近，继续向下的空间反而可能有限。

因为做市和期权结构会让这个位置变成一个很重要的博弈区间。

————————

再加上目前流通盘相对较少，真正大额解锁还需要一个多月。

所以现在的 SPCX，本质上形成了一个很适合交易的 PVP 环境：

流通盘不大，故事足够强，价格锚足够清晰，波动又足够大。

这也是为什么它能在大盘普跌的时候逆势上涨，甚至成交额超过 加密货币。

加密用户其实最懂这种结构。

大家交易的不是一句“长期看好”，而是流动性、筹码、价格锚、解锁节奏和对手盘。

以前这些东西更多发生在加密市场。

但现在 SPCX 这种资产，把美股的相对公平、真实公司叙事、马斯克流量和加密用户熟悉的 PVP 博弈结合到了一起。

所以我觉得，SPCX 成交额超过加密货币，不是偶然。

它说明资金正在从单纯情绪，转向更强叙事、更清晰筹码结构、更容易形成共识的超级资产。

这也是加密市场战略调整的必然。

SpaceX 本身就是全球最强的未上市公司之一。

而 SPCX 让普通用户第一次可以更直接地参与这类资产的交易。

这才是它真正能吸走加密市场注意力的原因。

The fastest chip no longer wins on its own. Training a big AI model means tens of thousands of GPUs all working on the same problem at once, and they have to constantly pass data back and forth to stay in sync. The network that carries that data now decides how fast the whole thing runs.

$NVDA says the old networking wasn't built for this. In their words, "Ethernet was designed primarily for enterprise applications" and "wasn't created for the synchronized, collective-heavy communication patterns of gigascale AI."

Amdahl's Law says a system is only as fast as its slowest shared step. You can add all the GPUs you want, but if they spend their time waiting on each other to exchange data, you hit diminishing returns fast. At this scale, that waiting happens in the network. So a faster chip can't outrun a fabric that can't feed it.

That's what Spectrum-6 is built to fix. It's a 102.4 Tb/s switch, double the last generation, made for NVIDIA's new Vera Rubin platform. NVIDIA claims up to 1.6x better AI networking performance than standard Ethernet, holding 95% efficiency even across 100,000-plus GPUs.

After the $SPCX IPO, the theme caught a lot of attention. So instead of chasing the name in the spotlight, I mapped the supply chain underneath it, from satellites down to minerals and everything in between.

The next space boom won't be won in space.

The global space economy hit $686B in 2025, up 12% in a year, with commercial activity at $544.3B of it. Space Foundation has it crossing $1.01 trillion by 2034.

Most of that money isn't made in space. Satellite-enabled products and services on the ground did $385.9B, roughly 71% of all commercial space revenue. Navigation, insurance, precision agriculture, logistics, aviation, broadband.

You think you have to be an astronaut to use these services? Think again. You're using them every day, in Google Maps.

Underneath that, the physical side is entering a real production phase. 2025 produced 317 orbital launches and 4,544 deployed spacecraft, up 25% and 54% versus 2024. Satellite manufacturing revenue grew 67.2%. Launch revenue grew 49.4%.

The line that matters most for this trade

Rockets got cheap and abundant. Launch infrastructure didn't keep up. Pads, ranges, integration facilities and coordination capacity have not moved anywhere near as fast as launch cadence.

Bottlenecks in an industrial buildout don't disappear. They migrate. Wherever the constraint lands next is where the pricing power goes.

That's the same reason I mapped twelve layers for AI. The visible company isn't always the bottleneck, and the best position usually sits a floor or two below the headline.

So here are the eight layers that are most relevant

L1 — Orbital Capacity, Data & Services. What customers actually buy. Broadband, mobility, earth observation, analytics, PNT, in-orbit services.

L2 — Networks, Fleets & Mission Operations. Constellations, mission control, capacity management, TT&C, data relay. Turning spacecraft into a service.

L3 — Finished Systems & Operational Assets. Launch vehicles, comms spacecraft, defense spacecraft, landers and servicers. The visible, qualified products.

L4 — Major Platform & System Elements. Launch stages, fairings and dispensers, spacecraft buses, payload modules.

L5 — Functional Subsystems & Assemblies. Propulsion and fluids, structures and mechanisms, power and thermal, avionics and GNC, payload assemblies.

L6 — Components, Electronics & Precision Parts. Compute and avionics, RF and interconnect, photonics and optics, propulsion hardware, structural and thermal. This is where the hidden bottlenecks live. A cheap part that can't be qualified delays an entire mission.

L7 — Engineered Materials & Mill Forms. Superalloys, composites, ablatives, electronic and optical materials, mill stock.

L8 — Critical Raw Materials. Structural and refractory metals, ceramics, semiconductor materials, rare earths, battery materials. This is what determines availability, geopolitical exposure, and the economics of expanding anything above it.

And four rails running alongside

Some capabilities don't sit inside the stack, they run beside it, and they can become bottlenecks in their own right.

Launch Services & Infrastructure. Pads, towers, propellant farms, integration facilities, range safety, recovery assets. The clearest evidenced bottleneck in the sector right now, and almost nobody has it on a list.

Ground Segment & User Access. Gateways, user terminals, mission control, network core. A gateway isn't made from satellites and a satellite isn't made from gateways, which is exactly why it gets filed under support infrastructure and ignored.

Manufacturing, Test & Qualification. Five-axis machining, autoclaves, thermal-vacuum chambers, vibration test, antenna ranges, engine test stands, radiation screening. Anyone can add a machine. Adding a machine whose output is certified to fly takes years.

Propellants & Consumables. LOX, methane, kerosene, hydrazine, xenon, krypton. Demand scales with how often you fly, not how many vehicles come off the line.

The honest part

With AI I have an unfair advantage. I run AI at a major enterprise, so I'm the customer and my suppliers tell me where the next constraint is forming before it shows up in a headline.

Space isn't my day job, I wish it was. What I have is a network inside the biggest space companies in the world and a framework, and the framework travels.

Also worth saying, the biggest blind spot in this map is vertical integration. At least one major player builds most of its own stack, and every layer it absorbs is a supplier that stops existing. A layered map is architecturally incapable of showing that. It's the weakness in my own framework and probably the most important competitive fact in the industry.

Even after being reviewed by friends who work at NASA and SpaceX, this can still be improved.

Just valuations and narratives (often noise) change, and markets rotate from sector to sector.

【美股复盘 · 8月11日】

**大市**

美股周二反复偏软，三大指数齐挫，惟小型股逆市造好，大市呈现明显的强弱分化。标普500(SPY)收报770.44,跌0.34%;纳指(QQQ)收报717.62,跌0.45%,科技权重股沽压最重;道指(DIA)收报537.49,跌0.28%。相反,罗素小型股(IWM)收报301.33,升0.45%,为四大指数中唯一收升者。市宽数据显示,75只观察股中41只上升、34只下跌,升跌比仍略偏好,反映跌市集中于个别重磅权重股,并非全面沽压。

**板块**

科网及AI基建下游股份领跌。数据中心与企业软硬件一线沽压沉重,甲骨文 $ORCL 急泻3.93%,戴尔 DELL 挫3.83%,两者跌幅相若;应用软件股 APP 重挫5.43%,为观察股中跌幅之冠;太空概念 SPCX 泻4.33%。大型科技股同告失守,谷歌 GOOGL 跌3.63%,阿里巴巴 BABA 跌3.41%,Netflix NFLX 跌2.11%,亚马逊 AMZN 跌2.09%,博通 AVGO 跌2.04%,巴郡 BRK-B 亦跌1.95%。

上游半导体及存储链则逆市造好,一枝独秀。荷兰光刻机龙头 ASML 升2.99%,存储股 SNDK 升3.42%、STX 升2.53%,数据中心电源设备股 VRT 升3.19%。此外,加密及另类资产概念 CRCL 大升5.91%领涨全场,AI云商 NBIS 升4.11%,通讯设备股 NOK 升3.72%,卫星通讯 ASTS 升3.68%,SKHY 升3.52%,量子计算 IONQ 升2.50%。

**焦点**

市场资金明显在AI产业链内部换位。同一轮资本开支,上游厂商属现金落袋,当季即见收入;下游数据中心营运商则须举债购置设备,自行承担折旧年期,再按合约价出租算力,backlog数字愈大,先行垫付的现金愈多。 ORCL 与 DELL 同日跌逾3.8%,两家主营业务相距甚远,惟资金来路一致——借贷兴建数据中心,赚取利差,在10年期国债孳息高企的环境下,分母持续构成压力,估值受压。相反, ASML 、 SNDK 、 STX 等上游厂商同日造好,资金取态一目了然。

另一条线索来自算力基建的实物资产。挖矿企业近年真正累积的并非币,而是电力资源——园区、变电站,尤其是并网排队位置,部分排期已至2029年,有资金亦难以插队。此批资产原为挖币而置,现已成AI数据中心的稀缺投入;近期已有矿企与AI公司签订大额算力合同。惟此概念亦有另一面,加密资产储备公司Twenty One Capital市值已低于其资产负债表上比特币的账面值,反映市场对"财资公司"模式的溢价正在收窄。

**小结**

全日观之,指数虽跌,但跌幅温和,市宽仍属健康,难言转势;真正发生的是AI产业链内部的一次资金再分配——由需要举债、迟收现金的下游,流向当季即可确认收入的上游。分析指,只要长息未见明显回落,下游数据中心营运商的估值压力将持续,而存储与半导体设备等"当季见钱"的环节相对占优。小型股 IWM 单日逆市走强,亦值得留意后市能否延续。
